transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main reason is I keep making these small mistakes that end up looking really bad. Like, I’ll turn in an application or some research notes, and I’ll be sure I checked it, but then there’s a skipped question or something mislabeled—like I put the wrong date on an artwork, which is especially embarrassing because I studied this stuff.

It’s not like I’m trying to be careless. I actually think I’m being careful, and then later I notice one of those little errors and it’s just… frustrating. That’s kind of what finally made me think I should come in.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or overly worried about making mistakes, even before you turn in your work?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think I’m sitting there panicking before I turn things in, exactly. Sometimes I’ll double-check because I know I’ve missed stuff before, but it’s more like… I’m trying to prevent the annoying thing from happening again.

Like, with applications, the forms all look the same after a while, and then I start thinking about whether I attached the right file, and then somehow I’m remembering this one museum catalog I had to use in college that had the dates formatted weirdly—sorry, that’s kind of not the point. I guess I notice the worry more after I find the mistake than before.
Do you often find yourself having thoughts that pop up unexpectedly and feel intrusive, like the example you gave about remembering a museum catalog when trying to focus on something else?

Yeah, kind of. I don’t know if I’d call them intrusive exactly, but when I’m trying to read or write at my desk, it doesn’t take much to pull me off track. Like a siren outside, or someone talking in the hallway, and then suddenly I’m thinking about that instead.

Or even just a random thought, like an exhibit idea or how something could be arranged in a gallery, and then I’ll sort of follow that thread. And then I look up and it’s been, like, twenty minutes and I haven’t actually gotten back to what I was doing.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, especially ones that aren’t very exciting or stimulating, like filling out forms or doing routine work?

Yeah, definitely. Forms and routine stuff are the worst for that. I’ll be trying to read something or write at my desk, and then a siren outside or someone talking in the hallway just pulls me away.

And sometimes it’s not even noise—it’ll be some random thought, like an exhibit idea or how a gallery could be laid out, and I follow that for a while. Then I sort of come back and realize it’s been twenty minutes and I haven’t done the thing I was supposed to be doing.
Outside of work or structured tasks, do you often find it hard to stay organized or follow through with things like chores, errands, or even just keeping track of your belongings?

Yeah, that happens. Not like my whole apartment is a disaster or anything, but I’ll mean to do normal stuff—return an email, pay a bill, pick up groceries—and then it just kind of… falls out of my head.

Like I’ll remember it at a weird time, maybe while I’m doing something else, and think, “Okay, I’ll do that later,” and then three days go by and I realize I never actually did it. Groceries especially, because I’ll think I can remember the couple things I need, and then I end up buying something random and forgetting the actual thing. Not always, but often enough that it’s annoying.

When did you first start noticing these kinds of difficulties—like trouble focusing, being easily distracted, or forgetting tasks? Did they start when you were a child, or was it more recently, like in adulthood?

I think it goes back pretty far, honestly. Like, elementary school kind of far.

I remember teachers writing stuff like I had good ideas, or that I was creative, but then there’d be this other part where I forgot to turn in worksheets, or I lost the instructions, or missed some little detail. My parents used to check my backpack every night, which was… I hated it at the time, because it felt like this whole inspection thing, but if they didn’t, something would usually be crumpled at the bottom or just not handed in.

So yeah, not just recently. It’s been around since I was a kid, I think.

Do these kinds of problems—like being distracted, forgetting tasks, or having trouble staying focused—happen in different parts of your life, such as at home, at work, and in other places like when you were in school?

I mean… I think so, but I’m not totally sure how to separate it out. Like, school definitely, because there were assignments and papers and all that structure, so it showed up there.

At home it’s more like little things, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing or just me being, I don’t know, kind of scattered sometimes. Work is harder to answer because I’m not really in a steady job situation right now, so I don’t want to say it shows up there in some big way.

But yeah, I guess it isn’t only one setting. It’s just easier to notice when there’s some system I’m supposed to be following. Like in school, or forms, or deadlines… sorry, I’m kind of circling it. I’d say it has happened in more than one part of my life, but I’m not sure how strongly.
Do you find these same kinds of problems—like being distracted or forgetting things—happen in social situations or with personal projects, not just with schoolwork or forms?

Yeah, I think it does. Like with personal projects especially. If I’m trying to read something or write at my desk, it doesn’t take much to knock me off track.

A siren outside, or someone talking in the hallway, or even just some random thought—like an idea for an exhibit or something—and then suddenly I’m not doing the thing anymore. I’ll follow that thought or look something up, and then it’s like twenty minutes have passed before I even realize I stopped.

Socially… I guess it can happen too, but I notice it more when I’m alone trying to actually do something.

Have these difficulties with focus, distraction, or forgetfulness ever caused problems in your relationships or with personal responsibilities, like missing appointments, forgetting plans with friends, or not following through on something important to you?

Yeah… I mean, not like huge disasters, but it has caused problems.

I’ve turned work in late because I thought I had more time or I just didn’t stay on top of it, and I’ve missed a couple application deadlines, which really bothered me because those were things I actually cared about. And then—this is kind of embarrassing—a mentor basically told me that my follow-through was starting to hurt opportunities I should’ve been ready for.

That one stuck with me, because I don’t think they were trying to be mean. It was more like… “you’re capable, but you’re not getting things in when you need to.” And I hate hearing that, because I know it’s probably true.

Can you describe a time when you tried to organize your tasks or set up a system to stay on track—like using reminders, planners, or to-do lists—and whether that helped you stay focused or complete what you needed to do?

Yeah, I’ve tried to set up systems. Like I’ll make a to-do list, or I’ll put reminders somewhere, and for a day or two it feels like, okay, this is the solution.

But then the list sort of becomes part of the mess. My apartment and my laptop both kind of look like… half-started projects everywhere. Rent papers mixed with gallery notes, article PDFs open in different tabs, random to-do lists in notebooks or on my desktop. And then I end up spending time reorganizing the system instead of actually doing the thing.

It’s not that I don’t know there are tasks. It’s more like I can’t always figure out what needs to happen first, so everything feels equally urgent or equally avoidable. Then I’ll start with one thing, notice another thing, and suddenly I’m just moving papers around or renaming folders instead of finishing anything.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be moving or doing something, especially when you're trying to focus or sit still for a period of time?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as especially restless in that way. Like, I can sit for a while if I have to.

Sometimes I’ll shift around or get up to get water or something, but… I don’t know if that’s more than normal. It’s funny, I notice the room more than my body, if that makes sense—like if there’s a weird noise from outside, I’ll start wondering where it’s coming from, and then I’m thinking about the street or what building it bounced off of, which is not really what you asked.

So, yeah… I guess I haven’t noticed a big “need to move” feeling. More just my attention going somewhere else.
Have you ever found yourself acting on impulse without thinking things through, like interrupting others, making sudden decisions without planning, or feeling like you can't wait your turn?

I don’t know… I don’t think that’s really my main thing. Like, I’m not usually the person who just jumps into a decision or can’t wait in line or whatever.

I might interrupt sometimes if I’m excited or if I’m worried I’ll lose what I was going to say, but even then I usually notice and feel awkward about it. Actually, that reminds me of seminars where I’m trying to hold a thought while someone else is talking, and then by the time it’s my turn the thought has kind of changed shape, or I’m thinking about some detail they mentioned instead of my original point.

But impulsive like suddenly doing big things without thinking them through… I don’t really see myself that way. I’d say I’m more likely to get stuck than to rush into something.

Have you ever felt an inner sense of restlessness, especially when you're supposed to be staying focused or still for a while—like your mind feels like it's constantly going a hundred miles an hour even if your body isn’t moving?

Maybe? I’m not sure I’d describe it as “a hundred miles an hour,” exactly. Sometimes my mind feels busy, but I don’t always know if that’s restlessness or just… thinking too much.

Like if I’m supposed to sit and focus, I might end up following one thought to another, and then suddenly I’m remembering some totally unrelated thing, like an email I didn’t answer or a line from something I read. But I don’t know if that’s an inner restless feeling. It’s more slippery than that, if that makes sense.

I guess I don’t really notice a strong internal “I need to move” feeling. More like my attention wanders off and I realize later I wasn’t really with what I was supposed to be doing.

These symptoms align with a presentation of Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation.
